blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Webcam eye tracking can greatly accelerate data collection in basic and applied research by reaching large, diverse samples of participants online. However, its spatial performance is considered well below that of hardware-based systems, limiting its use. We evaluated the first-generation Chiasm webcam eye tracker in a large online study ($N = 505$) spanning diverse participants, devices, and recording conditions. Chiasm achieved a mean spatial accuracy of 2.39 cm ($\approx 2.28^\circ$ at 60 cm), spatial precision (SD) of 1.05 cm ($\approx 1.00^\circ$ at 60 cm), and sample-to-sample precision (RMS-S2S) of 1.29 cm ($\approx 1.23^\circ$ at 60 cm). For the 91% of participants who met a 3 cm calibration criterion, spatial accuracy was 2.15 cm ($\approx 2.05^\circ$ at 60 cm). After three minutes of a task that encouraged head movement, spatial accuracy declined by 0.59 cm, while the gaze center at each target shifted by a mean distance of only 0.37 cm. On the validation block, the offset was 0.30 cm larger for men than for women. Age, region of residence, face luminance, and Michelson contrast showed no reliable relationship with spatial accuracy. A higher eye aspect ratio, a more open eye, was associated with a smaller offset. Wearing glasses decreased spatial accuracy on every validation block. In a comparison between a random subsample ($N = 101$) and a separate sample tested with the open-source tracker WebGazer ($N = 101$) using an identical protocol, Chiasm showed better spatial accuracy (2.18 vs. 4.51 cm) and spatial precision (SD; 1.01 vs. 1.55 cm). WebGazer showed better sample-to-sample precision (RMS-S2S; 0.79 vs. 1.26 cm), which likely reflects conservative, over-smoothed estimates rather than superior stability. These results suggest that Chiasm is narrowing the gap between webcam and hardware-based eye tracking, making large-scale gaze research "in the wild" a reality.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Eye tracking has proven to be a powerful tool for studying human behavior and cognition, with applications ranging from basic research to user experience (UX)
research, marketing, and clinical practice [ 26 , 19 , 16 , 6 , 21 , 24 , 7 , 1 , 12 , 23 , 20 , 29 , 10 , 2 , 3 , 8 ] . Yet its potential remains constrained by how difficult it is to collect large and diverse datasets.
Most eye tracking is still conducted in the lab, under controlled conditions, one participant at a time. Wearable eye trackers have relaxed some of these
constraints, but they still rely on specialized hardware that must be delivered to participants. Webcam eye tracking offers a way around this bottleneck by
using the commodity webcams built into virtually every laptop, tablet or smartphone. The idea is simple: anyone with such a device can take part in an eye-tracking experiment. Combined
with large, vetted online participant pools such as Prolific [ 13 ] , this shrinks data collection from weeks to hours.

blocks.en:
However, fulfilling this promise presents significant challenges, as data collection takes place “in the wild”, where researchers cannot control participants’
hardware, environment, or behavior. First, commodity webcams are far less capable than the cameras used in lab-based systems. They have lower spatial
resolution (often as low as 640 × 480 640\times 480 pixels, with the eye occupying only a small fraction of the image) and lower sampling rates (typically 30–60 Hz,
compared to 500–2000 Hz for lab systems such as the EyeLink 1000 Plus). They also lack infrared illumination, which rules out the pupil–corneal reflection
method on which most lab-based trackers rely. In addition, webcams apply automatic exposure, white balance, and compression that the experimenter cannot
control, and browsers introduce variable frame timing. The rest of the setup varies as well: computing hardware, operating systems, browsers, monitors,
and internet connections all differ across participants. Second, the recording environment is uncontrolled: ambient lighting, viewing distance,
and potential distractions vary from one participant to the next and can change during a session. Finally, there is no control over participants’ posture
and head movements, which are not constrained by a chin rest. Their engagement is also uncontrolled, and an experimenter cannot intervene in real time when
data quality deteriorates. These three major challenges for obtaining high-quality gaze data using webcam require not only a gaze estimation algorithm that
is robust to the variability in computing infrastructure, recording environment and participant behavior, but also a well-designed user interface that allows
self-guidance, feedback and error recovery for the participant, to compensate for the absence of an experimenter in the room.

blocks.en:
The most widely used webcam eye tracker is WebGazer [ 14 ] , an open-source, JavaScript library that detects the eyes in the webcam
image and maps eye-image features to screen coordinates using ridge regression, trained on clicks or gazing at calibration points. Several studies
estimated WebGazer’s spatial accuracy to be around 4 4 – 5 ∘ 5^{\circ} in the lab with further degradation online [ 18 ] . Most commercial
webcam eye
trackers, such as RealEye.io (based on WebGazer, [ 25 ] ) and LabVanced (deep learning-based, [ 11 ] ), have not been
validated “in the wild”, but rather under controlled and favourable conditions against lab-based systems, and reported spatial accuracy of around 1.5 ∘ 1.5^{\circ} .
One recent study [ 17 ] compared the performance of several deep learning-based models for gaze estimation (MPIIGaze [ 28 ] ,
ETHXGaze [ 27 ] and FAZE [ 15 ] ) on webcam frames collected online ( N = 65 N=65 ), but analyzed offline , in several tasks. They showed
that FAZE achieved the best performance, with a spatial accuracy of 2.44 ∘ 2.44^{\circ} and a spatial precision (SD) of 1.63 ∘ 1.63^{\circ} and RMS-S2S of 0.47 ∘ 0.47^{\circ} .
MPIIGAZe and ETHXGaze achieved a spatial accuracy of 3.70 ∘ 3.70^{\circ} and 3.40 ∘ 3.40^{\circ} , a spatial precision (SD) of 2.96 ∘ 2.96^{\circ} and 2.39 ∘ 2.39^{\circ} ,
and RMS-S2S of 2.33 ∘ 2.33^{\circ} and 1.80 ∘ 1.80^{\circ} respectively. The increased performance for different models came at the expense of inference time, with
inference latency of 12 fps for MPIIGaze, 4 fps for ETHXGaze and 1 fps for FAZE. Especially for FAZE, the most promising model, this means that all processing,
including the calibration procedure, has to be done offline, which may impair user experience and be impractical for some applications. It is worth noting
that this research evaluated the offline performance of several models on webcam data, but did not evaluate a webcam eye tracking system.

blocks.en:
There are a few reasons to suspect that the metrics that were previously reported for the webcam eye tracking may be rather optimistic. First,
most webcam eye trackers were tested under controlled laboratory conditions, which are not representative of diverse online scenarios [ 25 ] , [ 11 ] .
Second, in some studies, recalibration was often performed after short intervals, which was done to reduce the effect of drift over time,
but it is not always practical when running online [ 11 ] , [ 17 ] . Third, none of the studies estimated the drift in calibration metrics
over time, which is important to know and control for, as showed by [ 5 ] for the hardware-based eye trackers. Finally, many studies did not report
all the metrics that are crucial for the evaluation of the
webcam eye tracker’s performance, such as spatial accuracy, spatial precision (SD) and sample-to-sample precision (RMS-S2S) [ 18 ] , [ 9 ] .

blocks.en:
In this paper, we evaluated the first-generation Chiasm webcam eye tracker ( https://chiasm.eu ), which uses a deep neural network
to predict gaze from a single webcam image, combined with a custom calibration procedure. We conducted a large online study ( N = 505 N=505 ) spanning diverse
participants, devices, and recording conditions. We designed a novel validation protocol which allowed us to comprehensively evaluate the webcam
eye tracker’s performance “in the wild”. We report spatial accuracy, spatial precision (SD), sample-to-sample precision (RMS-S2S),
as well as drift of these metrics over time. In addition,
we evaluated how the tracker’s performance varies with different participant and environmental characteristics, such as age, gender, region of residence,
eye aspect ratio, face luminance, or Michelson contrast, and presence of glasses. We also compared the performance of Chiasm with WebGazer, since the latter is the most
widely used webcam eye tracker and could be implemented with an identical experimental protocol. We collected a separate sample with WebGazer ( N = 101 N=101 ) and
compared it with a random sample of participants from the Chiasm cohort.

blocks.en: 2 Methodology
blocks.zh: 2. 方法

blocks.en:
We used Chiasm’s implementation in jsPsych [ 4 ] and designed a novel experimental protocol that allowed us to compute various metrics of the webcam eye tracker’s
performance “in the wild”. First, we gave
participants three attempts to calibrate the tracker. This ensured that they had a chance to adjust to the calibration procedure and to give it their best
effort.
Second, even if they failed to calibrate the tracker after three attempts, we still allowed them to continue the session. This way we did not bias our
results by excluding participants who failed to calibrate the tracker.
Third, directly after the initial 9-point calibration and validation, which used pulsating discs, designed to attract attention, we presented participants with
a 13-dot validation block (Validation A), with static discs, which are commonly used in lab-based eye tracking.
Fourth, we presented participants with a shooting game, which encouraged them to move their head. Right after the shooting game, another 13-dot validation
block was presented (Validation B). This allowed us to assess the tracker’s drift over time and after head movements. The whole experiment lasted
approximately 14 minutes.

blocks.en: 2.1 Participants
blocks.zh: 2.1 与会者

blocks.en:
The complete dataset (Chiasm and WebGazer) was gathered from multiple participant batches over 12 days, totaling 36 hours of active collection time. Participants were
recruited via Prolific and gave informed consent. Data were processed under a data protection impact assessment (DPIA) by Chiasm B.V., in accordance with the General Data
Protection Regulation (GDPR). They took part remotely using a web browser. Participants using phones, tablets, iPadOS or Desktop Safari were not allowed to enter the
experiment.
Declining informed consent also ended the session, as did a failure to initialise the tracker. Participants who continued, reported whether the webcam was built-in,
external, or of unknown type; whether the computer was a laptop or a desktop; and whether the display was a laptop screen, an external monitor, or an all-in-one screen.

blocks.en: 2.2 Apparatus
blocks.zh: 2.2 设备

blocks.en:
Participants used their own webcam and display, without a chin rest, and viewing distance was left free. The sampling rate was capped at 30Hz and the frames were
rescaled to 640x480 pixels. Physical scale was obtained before calibration by matching an on-screen rectangle to a standard identification card, 85.6 mm wide. The match supplied a pixels-per-centimetre factor for the screen plane.
When the browser’s page zoom was away from 100%, a warning was shown and the participant could continue after resetting the zoom. The display was then placed in fullscreen. The tracker recorded webcam frames and the gaze prediction for each frame. The cursor was hidden during the validation blocks and the shooting game.

blocks.en: 2.3 Stimuli
blocks.zh: 2.3 刺激

blocks.en:
Calibration and its acceptance check used a 9-point grid on a white field: the screen center, the four edge midpoints, and the four corners. Peripheral points were inset
by 10% of screen width or height, and every point was kept at least 40 px inside the canvas. The center point appeared first; the other eight followed in random order.
Each point was combination of bulls eye and cross hair, known to minimize microsaccades [ 22 ] . Each point was a red disc that expanded from a radius
of 20 px to 40 px and then reset, crossed by a white cross 40 px across, with a red center of radius 4 px. The point stayed for 3.1 s. Samples entering the calibration
fit and its score began 800 ms after the point appeared.

以屏幕宽度或高度的10%表示,每个点至少保留在画布内40px. 中心点先出现;其他八个按随机顺序出现.
每个点都是牛眼和横毛的结合,已知可以将微saccades最小化[22]. 每个点都是从半径向外扩张的红盘
20 px到40 px,然后重置,由白色十字交叉40 px穿过,半径4 px的红色中心. 要点是3.1s。 进入校准的样本
它的得分从800米开始

blocks.en: Validation A and Validation B used thirteen points. The grid contained the same nine locations, placed at the 10% insets with no further edge margin, plus four inner points at 30% and 70% of screen width and height. Each block drew a new random order of all thirteen points. A point was a static red disc of radius 30 px, a white cross spanning the disc, and a red center of radius 4 px, on white. It stayed for 1.5 s, and the next point followed immediately. The recorded target was the center of the point in pixels of the current viewport.
blocks.zh: 验证A和验证B使用了13分. 网格包含相同的9个位置,布置在10%的插座上,没有进一步的边缘边距,外加4个内点,屏幕宽度和高度分别为30%和70%. 每个块绘制了所有13个点的新随机顺序. 一个点是半径30px的静态红盘,横跨圆盘的白色十字,以及半径4px的红色中心,在白色上. 它停留了1.5秒,接下来的一点紧接着。 所记录的目标是当前视点的像素中心.

blocks.en: Between the two validation blocks, participants played a shooting game and were encouraged to move their head.
blocks.zh: 在两个验证块之间,参与者玩射击游戏,被鼓励移动头部.

blocks.en: 2.4 Design
blocks.zh: 2.4 设计

blocks.en: The study was a single-group, within-participant validation with a fixed order. Every participant received the device check, consent, the device questionnaire, screen-size and camera setup, 9-point calibration with its acceptance check, Validation A, three rounds of a shooting game, a face-position check, Validation B, and a debrief. Validation B repeated Validation A after the shooting game. The acceptance check used the same 9-point routine as calibration and passed when the mean offset error was at most 3 cm. The setup could be repeated for up to three attempts. A failure to detect the face during the camera check did not use up an attempt. If the face was lost during calibration, the setup returned to the camera check and that restart counted. At the end of the setup the session continued whether or not the criterion had been met, and the outcome was stored. Validation instructions asked the participant to hold the head still and look at the center of each point. Instructions for the shooting game encouraged movement of the head as well as the eyes.
blocks.zh: 该研究为单组,参与者内部验证,定序. 每个参与者都收到设备检查,同意,设备问卷,屏幕尺寸和相机设置,9点校准其接受检查,验证A,三轮射击游戏,面部位置检查,验证B,以及汇报. 在射击游戏之后,验证B重复验证A. 验收检查使用与校准相同的9点常规,当平均抵消误差最多3厘米时通过. 这种设置最多可以重复三次。 在照相机检查时未能检测到面孔,没有使用尝试. 如果在校准时面部丢失,则布置返回到相机检查中,重新开始计算. 在设置结束时,会议继续举行,不论是否达到标准,结果已储存。 验证指示要求参与者把头按住,并查看每个点的中心. 对射击游戏的指示鼓励了头部和眼睛的运动.

blocks.en: 2.5 Procedure
blocks.zh: 2.5 程序

blocks.en:
After a welcome page, participants gave informed consent and completed the device questionnaire. Setup instructions asked them to sit comfortably and keep the head still.
They matched the on-screen card to a physical card, made sure their face was centered on the camera image, and entered fullscreen.
Calibration and the acceptance check followed, each introduced with the instruction to follow each point with the eyes. Validation A was introduced with the instruction to look at the center of each point and keep the head still. Fullscreen was requested again, and the thirteen points were shown. Participants then read the shooting-game instructions and played three rounds. They were encouraged to move their head during the game. Each round restated the aiming instruction, requested fullscreen, counted down from three, and lasted 60 s, after which a score summary was shown. Before Validation B the camera image was shown again so the participant could place the face in the oval. A failure of that check was recorded and the session continued into Validation B, which repeated the thirteen-point procedure. A final page returned the participant to Prolific. Figure 1 shows this order.

他们将屏幕卡与物理卡匹配,确保他们的脸以镜头图像为中心,并进入全屏.
随后进行了校准和验收检查,每次检查都指示眼睛跟随每个点。 验证 引入了A,指示查看每个点的中心,保持头部不动. 再次要求全屏,13分显示. 随后学员们阅读射击比赛指示,并进行了三轮比赛. 比赛期间鼓励他们移动头部. 每回合均重述瞄准指示,要求全屏,从3次倒计时,持续60秒,之后显示分数汇总. 验证前 B镜头画面再次显示,这样参与者就可以将面孔放入椭圆形. 核查失败,会议继续进入B号验证,重复了13点程序。 最后一页将参与者送回了Prolific. 图1显示了这一顺序。

blocks.en: 2.6 Data Filtering
blocks.zh: 2.6 数据过滤

blocks.en: Gaze is reported in centimetres in the screen plane, using the scale from the card match. Within each validation point, samples from the first 500 ms after onset were discarded. A sample was then discarded when it jumped more than 5 cm from the last kept sample at that point. Exact repeats of a gaze position within the same session and phase were discarded, keeping the first. Samples farther than three robust standard deviations from the median gaze at that point were also discarded. The robust standard deviation is 1.4826 times the median absolute deviation of distances to that median. Points with fewer than five finite samples, and points whose median absolute deviation was zero, were left untrimmed.
blocks.zh: 盖兹在屏幕平面中以厘米表示报告,使用从卡片对齐的尺度. 在每个验证点内,头500毫秒之后的样品被丢弃。 然后,当样品从最后保存的样品跳出5厘米以上时,样品被丢弃。 在同一会话中重复凝视位置的准确性被放弃,从而保留了第一个。 超过当时中位视差三个强烈标准偏差的样本也被丢弃。 坚固的标准偏差是距离与该中位数的绝对偏差的1.4826倍. 不超过5个有限样本的点和绝对偏差中位数为零的点没有调整。

blocks.en: 2.7 Evaluation metrics
blocks.zh: 2.7 评价尺度

blocks.en: A person-level value in a phase is the mean of the finite per-point values. It is left undefined when fewer than 9 points on a thirteen-point grid, or fewer than six on the 9-point grid, yield a finite value.
blocks.zh: 处于一个阶段的人级值是每点限值的平均值. 当十三分网格上不足九分,或九分网格上不足六分,产生有限值时,则未定义.

blocks.zh: 空间精确度

blocks.zh: 漂流

blocks.en: On the grid, the predicted center at a point is the median, across people, of the median gaze displacement from the target. Drift is the vector from that center on Validation A to the center on Validation B. Per person, drift is Validation B spatial accuracy minus Validation A spatial accuracy.

blocks.en: CDF
blocks.zh: 综合发展框架

blocks.en: The cumulative distribution function is the empirical distribution of per-person spatial accuracy, one value per phase. The denominator is the final sample. A person without a finite spatial accuracy stays in that denominator and does not add a step to the curve.

blocks.en: 2.8 Demographics and frame statistics
blocks.zh: 2.8 人口和框架统计

blocks.en: Spatial accuracy on the 9-point validation block was compared across gender, region of residence, and age. Gender was tested with a Welch t t -test of Male versus Female. Region and age were tested with one-way analyses of variance. Age was binned as 18–24, 25–34, 35–44, 45–54, and 55+. A region or age bin entered its analysis only when it contained at least two people. The same accuracy was also compared across the device questionnaire with Welch t t -tests of laptop versus desktop, built-in versus external webcam, and laptop screen versus external monitor. A person with fewer than six usable points was left out of these tests.
blocks.zh: 9点验证块的空间精确度在性别、居住区域和年龄方面进行了比较。 性别测试用Welch t t测试“男性对女性”。 对地区和年龄进行了单向差异分析。 年龄为18–24,25–34,35–44,45–54,55+. 只有当一个地区或年龄本包含至少两个人时,才输入其分析. 在整个设备问卷中,同样准确性也与Welch t t T对台式计算机的测试、内置与外部网络摄像头的测试、以及笔记本电脑屏幕与外部显示器的测试进行了比较。 在这些测试中,有一个不到6个可用点的人被排除在外。

blocks.en: The same spatial accuracy was related to the frame statistics on each validation phase. Presence of glasses, eye aspect ratio, face luminance, and contrast were automatically extracted from the frames. Glasses were tested with a 2 × 3 2\times 3 analysis of variance, glasses between subjects and validation block within subjects. Eye aspect ratio, face luminance, and Michelson contrast were each tested with a multiple regression of spatial accuracy in centimetres on that measure, validation block, a fixed person intercept, and the measure × \times block interaction.
blocks.zh: 同样的空间精确度与每个验证阶段的帧统计有关。 眼镜的存在,眼睛的尺寸比,面部亮度,对比度都自动从帧中提取出来. 眼镜通过2×3 2\times 3分析对象之间的差异,眼镜以及主体内的验证块来测试. 眼睛外观比,面部光亮度,Michelson对比度均通过该测量上空间精度的多次回归来测试,验证块,固定人截取,测量×\times块相互作用.

blocks.en: 2.9 Comparison with WebGazer
blocks.zh: 2.9 与WebGazer的比较

blocks.en:
We chose the WebGazer implementation in jsPsych [ 4 ] , since it is the most widely used implementation of WebGazer. It uses a 9-point calibration block, during which
participants are asked to click calibration dots, one by one, in a random order, with each location appearing two times. The calibration block is followed
by a 9-point validation block, during which participants are asked to look at the center of each dot for 2 seconds, with recording starting after 1 second.
blocks.zh:
我们在jsPsych [4]中选择了WebGazer执行,因为它是WebGazer最广泛使用的执行. 它使用9分校准区块,在此期间
请参与者按随机顺序单击校准点,每个位置出现两次。 校准块被遵循
由9点验证块进行,期间请参与者查看每个点的中心2秒,1秒后开始录音.

blocks.en:
The WebGazer dataset was collected using an identical experimental protocol on an independent sample of participants ( N = 101 N=101 ). The Chiasm dataset was a random
draw from the included sessions, matched in size to the WebGazer study.
Each dataset used the same procedure for data filtering. Chiasm discarded the first 500 ms after onset on every phase.
WebGazer kept every sample on the 9-point block and discarded the first 500 ms on Validation A and Validation B.
blocks.zh:
WebGazer数据集是使用一个独立的参与者样本(N=101 N=101)上相同的实验协议采集的. Chiasm 数据集是随机的
从包含的会话中提取,大小与WebGazer研究相匹配.
每个数据集都采用了相同的数据过滤程序. Chiasm在每个阶段发作后抛弃了前500毫秒.
WebGazer将每个样本保存在9点块上,并丢弃了在验证A和验证B上的前500ms.

blocks.en: The two datasets were compared on the evaluation metrics. For spatial accuracy, spatial precision (SD), and sample-to-sample precision (RMS-S2S), a planned independent-samples t t -test compared the trackers on each task. A 2 × 3 2\times 3 analysis of variance then tested tracker, between subjects, by task, within subjects. A person missing any task was left out of that analysis of variance.
blocks.zh: 在评价指标上比较了这两个数据集。 对于空间精度,空间精度(SD)和样本至样本精度(RMS-S2S),计划进行的独立样本 t - t - 测试,比较每项任务的跟踪器. 2×3 2\times 3 分析然后测试的跟踪器,按任务划分,在主体内. 在对差异的分析中,遗漏了一个人。

blocks.en:
The datasets were compared on demographics and frame statistics. Region of residence, gender, age, and glasses were tested with chi-square tests.
Face luminance, Michelson contrast, and eye aspect ratio were tested with Welch t t -tests.
blocks.zh:
对数据集进行了人口统计和框架统计的比较。 居住区、性别、年龄和眼镜都经过了Chi-quare测试。
面部亮度,Michelson的对比度,眼睛的视宽比都通过Welch t - t测试.

blocks.en: 3.2 Spatial precision (SD)
blocks.zh: 3.2 空间精确度(SD)

blocks.en:
In order to visualize the typical within-person spread of gaze at each validation point, we computed the covariance of the samples around that point’s own centroid for each point and for each participant (Figure 4 ). Spatial precision (SD) is the root mean square of that spread. The contour is the central 50% of a bivariate t t distribution with 5 degrees of freedom, centered on the true target and scaled by the median of these covariances across participants. It shows the typical size and tilt of the within-person scatter, separately from where the gaze landed.
The median spatial precision (SD), across participants and points, was 0.95 cm on the validation block (9-point), 0.97 cm on Validation A (13 points), and 0.99 cm on Validation B (13 points). The later blocks were only slightly less precise than the validation block. The contours extend farther vertically than horizontally, so spatial precision seems better in the horizontal dimension than in the vertical.
blocks.zh:

跨越参与者和点的中位空间精度(SD)在验证块(9-点)上为0.95厘米,在验证A(13点)上为0.97厘米,在验证B(13点)上为0.99厘米. 后期区块的精确度仅略低于验证区块. 轮廓垂直延伸较横向远,因此空间精度在水平维度上似乎优于垂直.

The mean was 1.05 cm on the validation block, 1.08 cm on Validation A, and 1.11 cm on Validation B. A repeated-measures analysis of variance of validation block, using the 490 people with a value on every block, was reliable, F ⁡ ( 2,978 ) = 19.86 F(2,978)=19.86 , p < 0.001 p<0.001 . blocks.en: 3.3 Sample-to-sample precision (RMS-S2S)
blocks.zh: 3.3 样本至样本精度(RMS-S2S)

blocks.en:
In order to measure how far gaze moved from one sample to the next, we computed the root mean square of the Euclidean distances between successive kept samples at each point and for each participant. Each person then contributes one value per phase: the mean of that person’s per-dot values. There must be at least six usable points on the validation block and at least nine on Validation A and Validation B in order to be included.
The mean was 1.29 cm on the validation block, 1.34 cm on Validation A, and 1.36 cm on Validation B. A repeated-measures analysis of variance of validation block, using the 490 people with a value on every block, was reliable, F ⁡ ( 2,978 ) = 23.17 F(2,978)=23.17 , p < 0.001 p<0.001 . Planned paired t t -tests distinguished the validation block from Validation A, t = − 6.01 t=-6.01 , d ​ f = 497 df=497 , p < 0.001 p<0.001 . Validation A and Validation B did not differ, t = − 1.75 t=-1.75 , d ​ f = 492 df=492 , p = 0.080 p=0.080 . This shows a small decrease in sample-to-sample precision from the validation block to Validation A, and no further change on Validation B.

A和验证B没有区别, t = - 1.75 t = 1.75, d f = 492 df = 492, p = 0.080 p = 0.080. 这表明从验证块到验证A的样本至样本精度略有下降,在验证B上没有进一步变化.

blocks.en:
In order to visualize how the predicted center moved from Validation A to Validation B, we drew one arrow at each of the 13 validation points (Figure 5 ). The tail is the predicted center on Validation A and the head is the predicted center on Validation B, the same center as the diamond in Figure 2 . The arrows are drawn at seven times their length for better readability. All 13 points had at least nine participants on both blocks (504 on Validation A and 501 on Validation B).
The mean shift across these points was − 0.00 -0.00 cm horizontally and 0.27 cm upward. The 0.37 cm in the abstract is the mean length of these shifts: at each of the 13 points, the distance from the Validation A predicted center to the Validation B predicted center, then the average of those 13 distances. A one-sample t t -test found no reliable horizontal shift, t = − 0.02 t=-0.02 , d ​ f = 12 df=12 , p = 0.99 p=0.99 . The upward shift was reliable, t = 4.34 t=4.34 , d ​ f = 12 df=12 , p < 0.001 p<0.001 . This shows a small upward shift of the predicted center, and no horizontal shift.

blocks.en: 4 Discussion
blocks.zh: 讨论

blocks.en:
The results from our large-scale validation study ( N = 505 N=505 ) show that Chiasm performs better than existing solutions “in the wild”, where the experimenter has no control over the devices, environment or
the participant’s behavior. The participants came from a diverse population in terms of region of residence, gender, age, and used a variety of devices. Our comprehensive
analysis showed that Chiasm has a spatial accuracy (2.39 cm) and precision (SD 1.05 cm), and the sample-to-sample
precision (1.29 cm) is also reasonable given the 30Hz sampling rate. These evaluation metrics improved slightly when only the participants who passed the calibration
were included in the analysis (see Table 1 ). The spatial accuracy and precision (SD) decreased over time, but the sample-to-sample precision
was more stable. The drift over time was small and directed upward and toward the center of the screen, which is consistent with regression to the center of the screen [ 17 ] .
Interestingly, the spatial accuracy decreased sharply from the validation block to Validation A, but only slightly to Validation B. This is likely due to the switch from
using dynamic to static targets. In validation block, the targets were pulsating discs, which captured participants’ attention in automatic fashion. In Validation A
and Validation B, the same discs, but static, which required more effort from the participants to track. While such static discs are the most common type of calibration
targets, they are probably not the most effective way to enforce fixation. Given that participants were not trained in eye-tracking tasks,
and did not receive feedback from the experimenter, this is not surprising that the spatial accuracy decreased.

In terms of external variables affecting spatial accuracy, the presence of glasses and the lower eye aspect ratio had substantial detrimental effects. The face luminance
or contrast had no effect on spatial accuracy. The demographic variables also had no effect on spatial accuracy, except for gender.
Chiasm’s spatial accuracy is comparable to the iMotions white paper report (median of 2.1 ∘ 2.1^{\circ} ), which is the only other large-scale validation study conducted
“in the wild” ( N = 255 N=255 ). They also found the effect of glasses to be detrimental. Unfortunately, the iMotions study did not report other metrics and were not clear about
the exact experimental setup.

Chiasm also outperformed the FAZE model, which included user-specific calibration [ 17 ] , but was run fully offline, on both spatial
accuracy of 2.28 ∘ 2.28^{\circ} vs 2.44 ∘ 2.44^{\circ} and a spatial precision (SD) of 1.00 ∘ 1.00^{\circ} vs 1.63 ∘ 1.63^{\circ} . Since the dataset on which FAZE was evaluated
excluded participants with glasses, Chiasm’s advantage over FAZE may be underestimated. FAZE yielded a lower RMS-S2S than our system
( 0.47 ∘ 0.47^{\circ} vs. 1.23 ∘ 1.23^{\circ} ). This difference likely reflects offline temporal smoothing of the gaze estimates by the Kalman filter in the
FAZE pipeline. In addition, Chiasm runs online with a near real-time inference speed, while FAZE requires fully offline processing. Interestingly,
in that study [ 17 ] , running the models fully offline on webcam frames collected online , resulted in high attrition,
since only 65 out of 118 participants were included in the analysis. This illustrates a limitation of fully offline processing, and emphasizes the importance
of user interface design for online gaze tracking.

Overall, we present a rigorous, comprehensive and extensive evaluation of Chiasm’s performance “in the wild”, as well as its comparison with WebGazer. Besides evaluating
it on all standard metrics such as spatial accuracy, spatial precision (SD), and sample-to-sample precision (RMS-S2S), we also evaluated it on drift of these metrics over
time, which gives a realistic picture of the tracker’s performance in a real-world scenario.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
In this study, which to our knowledge is the largest validation of a webcam-based
gaze tracker under unconstrained “in the wild” conditions to date
( N = 505 N=505 ), Chiasm achieved a mean spatial accuracy of approximately 2.3 ∘ 2.3^{\circ} of visual angle. This outperforms WebGazer, which we evaluated
directly, and compared favourably with previously reported webcam-based accuracies.
Chiasm thus narrows the gap to laboratory-based eye trackers: remote video-based trackers achieve about 0.5 ∘ 0.5^{\circ} under optimal
conditions, and wearable eye trackers typically around 1.5 ∘ 1.5^{\circ} [ 5 ] . A direct comparison with a laboratory
eye tracker under controlled conditions, ideally with simultaneous recording,
will be an important next step. We are confident that Chiasm is
ready to be used in a variety of real-world tasks, relying on multiple areas of interest (AOIs),
that are currently mainly performed in the lab. Chiasm is now available as an extension to jsPsych [ 4 ] , making it easy to use in a wide
range of research and applications.
